newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch VNU declines comment on Blenheim bid reports.
newsitem.headline: Dutch VNU declines comment on Blenheim bid reports.

text.p: Dutch publisher VNU on Monday declined comment on reports it was poised to boost its stake in British exhibitions group Blenheim to 25 percent.
"We cannot respond to rumours," spokesman Maarten Schikker said, adding: "All I can say is that we will consider the acquisition of further shares in Blenheim in the future."
British daily The Times said on Monday that VNU, which bought its current 15 percent holding in Blenheim last week, was planning to buy a further 10 percent stake.
Schikker declined to confirm or deny the report.

The paper quoted one of VNU's advisers as saying buying more shares was "a very real option" but could be scuppered if, as reported earlier, United News & Media tabled a 520p per share bid for Blenheim. VNU bought its stake for 500p a share.
"VNU will consider what action to take if and when these rumours are confirmed, but to comment now would be highly premature," Schikker said.

VNU said last week its acquisition of a 15 percent holding in Blenheim was a strategic long-term investment, and said it had no intention of making an offer for the whole company, unless rival offers for the firm emerged.
